title: A Rock and a Farway

beats.what: Frank's remains are carried out after his night in the box; the creatures left little
Jade insists on seeing where the dead man lay in the tunnel; there is nothing there now
Victor shows Ethan his crayon drawing of the boy who lives outside; Ethan confirms it is the same figure he saw
Jim confronts Tabitha with Tabitha's revelation that Julie knows about the planned divorce
Khatri confronts Boyd about punishing himself; names a dead woman as the grief Boyd cannot process
Victor leads Ethan to a farway tree, a branch that teleports objects to unpredictable locations
Ethan vanishes while Victor and Ethan examine the farway tree; parents discover he is gone
Boyd speaks to a grave, reveals tremors in his hand matching his father's illness, discloses his plan to get people home

character_beats.beat: Wants to be emotionally unavailable and purely functional yet cannot stop talking to a dead woman's grave; the tremors make his denial of grief both poignant and urgent
Wants to keep the family unit together yet goes to confront Julie alone without telling Jim, choosing individual action over the united front she argues for
Has abandoned the escape-room theory but replaced it with a new delusion: that someone designed this and can be reasoned with; his map of origins is the episode's intellectual substitute for grief

key_lines.why: Khatri's closing line names the unnamed woman as the wound driving Boyd; it reframes every prior Boyd scene

key_lines.line: I don't just sit around accepting the world as it is! Someone is doing this.
key_lines.why: Jade's refusal to adapt is his clearest statement of the show's alternative survival posture

key_lines.line: Thomas is dead. You have two other kids. Why aren't we enough for you?
key_lines.why: Julie names the dead brother Thomas; first confirmation the Matthews family grief predates the town

key_lines.line: Sometimes you end up stuck inside a mountain somewhere. They're temperamental that way.
key_lines.why: Victor's casual warning about the farway trees introduces teleportation risk just before Ethan uses one

open_loops: Where did Ethan teleport to via the farway tree?
Who is the unnamed woman Boyd grieves, and how did she die?
Who is Thomas and what happened to him before the family trip?
How many farway trees exist in the town, and who knows about them?
What is Boyd's plan that requires a 'big swing' and could leave people worse off?

payoffs.what: Victor's tree-measurement obsession from E03 is contextualized: he has been tracking the farway trees, not just proximity of the forest
The mysterious boy Ethan saw in E03 is confirmed real by Victor's crayon drawing matching Ethan's description

contradiction.wants: To hold himself to pure function and duty, no grief allowed
contradiction.does: Visits a grave alone, confesses tremors, admits to needing a sign, and asks a dead person for permission to act

tone_notes: The episode contains the batch's longest silence at 174 seconds (01:45-04:39), a long cold open that holds on Frank's aftermath without dialogue. A second silence of 136 seconds (36:22-38:38) follows the farway tree sequence as Ethan vanishes, letting the panic build without spoken words. Density peaks at minutes 22-23 (179 w/min) during the Jade mapping scene. Minutes 37-38 drop to zero, making Ethan's disappearance purely physical.
